finalMessage:
`Refunder.Refund` (payments/refund.go) exists to implement three requirements. I got this from `ostf context payments/refund.go#Refunder.Refund` and `trace.yaml`. I didn't read the function body or run the tests.

**Why it exists**

- **R-REFUND-LIMIT** is the main reason, and it is marked risk-relevant, so you must be asked before it is changed. A refund must not exceed what is left of the original charge. Refunds above 500.00 in one UTC day for an account need a second approval. It controls RISK-REFUND-ABUSE (a compromised account or a mistaken operator drains funds through refunds). It refines N-REFUNDS: customers get refunds quickly without the business losing money to abuse.
- **R-AUDIT-MONEY** says every charge and every refund appends an audit entry with the time, account, action, amount and receipt. It refines N-ACCOUNT-SAFE.
- **R-REFUND-ORIGINAL** says a refund goes back to the payment method of the charge it refunds, never to another one. It refines N-REFUNDS.

**Which tests cover it**

- `payments/refund_test.go#TestCheckRefundLimit` covers R-REFUND-LIMIT.
- `payments/refund_test.go#TestRefundDailyLimit` also covers R-REFUND-LIMIT, for the daily threshold.
- `payments/refund_test.go#TestRefund` covers R-AUDIT-MONEY and R-REFUND-ORIGINAL.
- `payments/charge_test.go#TestChargeAudited` covers the charge side of R-AUDIT-MONEY. It doesn't test `Refund`.

The trace links the limit requirement's code to `CheckRefundLimit`, not to `Refund` itself. The tests named for the limit therefore exercise the check, and `TestRefundDailyLimit` is the only one named for the daily rule. All the links `ostf context` printed show as valid.
